Subject: Capacity ask: mapping DEAL-9482 to Q4 Reserved GPUs

Anna / Acme procurement team —

Following up from last week’s pipeline review: Acme expects to convert DEAL-9482 (pilot -> production) with an initial committed volume of ~1.2k A100-equivalent GPUs across year 1, with a Q4 ramp target for 400 reserved GPUs for low-latency private deployment. We need to map that to our Dedicated capacity planning and confirm whether OEM manufacturing + cloud reserve options can meet an Oct/Nov onboard window.

Key asks:
- Can OEM provide an indicative lead time and partial-shipment cadence for a 400-unit order? (any components or sub-assembly constraints we should expect)
- Are there options for a staggered delivery (e.g., 50/150/200) to unblock canary capacity?
- If OEM lead times extend beyond Oct, what are cloud vendor bridge options (reserved temporary pools) and pricing?

I’ve attached a draft mapping (capacity_plan_v2.xlsx) that proposes which clusters get pinned to this deal; Marissa / Vivek — please review allocation assumptions and flag any constraints or alternative bridges.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the details. Summary from manufacturing: current baseline lead time for the chassis+accelerator assembly is ~18 weeks from PO receipt for standard builds. We can do a partial shipment path: first tranche (up to 50 units) in ~6–8 weeks if parts are available; the remainder in 2 subsequent tranches spaced 6–8 weeks apart. That assumes no last-minute BOM changes and an agreed payment schedule.

Notes and options:
- Expedited slots: we can pursue a 30% expedite surcharge to shorten full order to ~12 weeks, but capacity is limited and requires firm PO and 50% deposit.
- Buffer: recommend planning for 10–15% overcommit to account for DOA/validation failures.
- Firmware/config: we can ship with minimal firmware and a later OTA to avoid manufacturing delay — this reduces initial validation lead time but requires on-site config during onboarding.

I’ve attached our formal quote (OEM_quote_AnnaBosch_20260810.pdf) with line items and T&Cs. Happy to hop on a call to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,
Anna Bosch
Head of Supply Partnerships
OEM Solutions Ltd.

Thanks Anna — useful detail. Internal notes / proposal:

1) Allocation model
- Q4 target: reserve 400 units for Acme (DEAL-9482) across two clusters (east-us-prod, west-us-prod) for geographic redundancy.
- Canary tranche: request first 50 units from OEM partial-shipment to stand up east-us-prod and run canary traffic (low-risk, on-prem private deployment).

2) Buffering / bridging
- Plan a 12% operational buffer (48 units) to cover validation DOA + burn-in.
- Cloud bridge: we can lease up to 200 temporary GPUs from our cloud partner (supply@cloudvendor.com) for up to 12 weeks; cost estimate in sheet. This should cover the rest of the ramp if OEM full delivery slips.

3) Procurement timeline (internal)
- Freeze final BOM & submit PO to OEM by 2026-08-21 to hit the optimistic 18-week window.
- If PO delayed beyond 08/28, we recommend activating cloud bridge and negotiating expedited slot with OEM (30% surcharge).

Next steps: Jordan — can you confirm Acme’s PO intent/target date? Vivek — need your signoff on the cloud bridge ceiling (200 GPUs) and whether finance can approve the estimated bridge spend as a contingency. Karthik — please add this to the Dedicated capacity board and tag INF-4021.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Dedicated Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
